youtube.title: America Went to War Over an Attack That Never Happened | Gulf of Tonkin
youtube.description:
On 4 August 1964, two US destroyers in the Gulf of Tonkin, USS Maddox and USS Turner Joy, reported a night torpedo attack by North Vietnamese boats. President Johnson ordered retaliatory airstrikes, and on 7 August Congress passed the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution (416–0 in the House, 88–2 in the Senate), giving him broad power to wage war in Vietnam. In a study first published in NSA's classified Cryptologic Quarterly and declassified in 2005, NSA historian Robert J. Hanyok concluded that no attack happened that night, and that the signals intelligence given to officials was skewed to support the claim of an attack. (A first clash, on 2 August, did take place.)

📂 Case File #024: The Gulf of Tonkin

Sources: Robert J. Hanyok, "Skunks, Bogies, Silent Hounds, and the Flying Fish: The Gulf of Tonkin Mystery, 2-4 August 1964", NSA (declassified 2005), via the National Security Archive; National Security Archive Electronic Briefing Book No. 132; Britannica, "Gulf of Tonkin Resolution".
Images (Wikimedia Commons, public domain): U.S. Navy (USS Maddox, USS Turner Joy); LBJ Library / Cecil Stoughton (President Johnson).
Narration voice: AI.
